text: On 5 November 2026, France’s interior ministry said more than 600,000 people marched nationwide, with 70,000 police officers deployed and 448 arrests, and the Eiffel Tower was closed. The ministry’s figures contrast with the CGT’s claim of 1.6 million participants, and about a third of high schools were reported closed or unable to operate.

sources.title: More than 600,000 rally across France to demand higher wages and school funding - CTV News

More than 600,000 rally across France to demand higher wages and school funding
Protestetors walk during a demonstration demanding higher wages and supporting high school protest movement, in Lyon, France, Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026. (AP Photo/Laurent Cipriani)
PARIS -- Protest marches drew huge crowds Thursday in Paris and elsewhere across France as demonstrators demanded higher wages and backed the country’s student protest movement, piling fresh pressure on the beleaguered government.
France’s Interior Ministry said more than 600,000 people took to the streets while the CGT, one of France’s major unions, said nearly 1.6 million people took part in over 200 demonstrations nationwide. The figures exceed those reported on Oct. 17, when protests were marred by scenes of rioting and looting.
